text:
emma: AcmeCorp started seeing 401s for SSO logins right after their IdP metadata rotation (~09:18 UTC). SP logs show Recipient mismatch and signature verification failures. Pasting the short logs and what we've tried so far.

saml-checker-bot: Detected metadata update for idp.acme.com at 2026-03-10T09:18:23Z; new KeyDescriptor ordering observed, includes both SHA1 and SHA256 certs. New signing cert fingerprint SHA256=FF:EE:DD:CC:BB:AA:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:00. Also metadata contains an AssertionConsumerService entry pointing to https://acme.app:443/sso/consume.

raj: Which env is this (prod/staging)? Can you paste the sanitized SAML Response snippet and the relevant SP log lines? Any RelayState or proxy in the flow?

emma: Prod. Repro steps from the customer: 1) User clicks SSO on our login page 2) Redirects to IdP and user authenticates 3) IdP POSTs SAML Response back to ACS 4) Browser receives 401 and user sees "Authentication failed".

emma: Relevant SP log snippet:
```
[auth-sp] 2026-03-10T09:20:01Z ERROR VerifyAssertion: Recipient mismatch: got 'https://acme.app:443/sso/consume' expected 'https://app.redwood.com/sso/acs'
[auth-sp] 2026-03-10T09:20:01Z ERROR InvalidSignature: signature verification failed: no matching cert found
```

emma: Sanitized SAML response fragment (subject confirmation):
```xml
<samlp:Response ...>
  <saml:Assertion>
    <saml:Subject>
      <saml:SubjectConfirmation>
        <saml:SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://acme.app:443/sso/consume" NotOnOrAfter="2026-03-10T09:25:01Z" />
      </saml:SubjectConfirmation>
    </saml:Subject>
    <ds:Signature>...signature blob...</ds:Signature>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
```

raj: Looks like the IdP is sending the ACS with an explicit port and a different host/path than our configured ACS. Did the customer recently add a proxy/ingress in front of the app that rewrites host/port?

oliver: I inspected the metadata we fetched: they added a new AssertionConsumerService with index=0 and isDefault=true pointing at https://acme.app:443/sso/consume. Previously our matching succeeded because the IdP used our canonical ACS URL. Our verifier matches Recipient exactly to configured SP ACS. Also the KeyDescriptor order changed (first entry is legacy SHA1 cert, second is SHA256).

emma: What we've tried so far:
- Forced metadata refresh and cleared auth-service cache (no change)
- Requested IdP rollback; they said rotation can't be undone
- Temporarily added an alternate_acs entry for this tenant with 'https://acme.app:443/sso/consume' — that reduced errors but ~20% still fail with signature errors

saml-checker-bot: Noted mix of signatures in logs: some assertions signed with the second (SHA256) key, others signed with the first (SHA1) key. Our verifier currently selects the first KeyDescriptor from metadata for verification, which is the SHA1 cert in this rotation. We reject SHA1-signed assertions. Fingerprints observed: SHA1=11:22:33..., SHA256=FF:EE:DD...

raj: Options: 1) Make the SP verification try all KeyDescriptor entries instead of assuming order (config toggle) 2) Ask IdP to publish only the SHA256 key or reorder KeyDescriptor so strongest key is first 3) Add tenant-specific accept_all_idp_keys flag while we patch verifier. Which is quickest to unblock users?

oliver: We can push a small config change to auth-service to accept all keys for a tenant (no code change) and then follow up with a proper verifier fix (try all keys, unit tests). I can prepare the patch; ETA ~3h for the code fix, config change is immediate. We'll do a canary for Acme first.

deploy-bot: Deploy request created: auth-service config update 'accept_all_idp_keys=true' for tenant=acmecorp. CI passed. Targeted canary ready (10% traffic).

emma: Rolling canary now. I'll monitor error rate and signature failures. Also CS is contacting the IdP admin to canonicalize ACS and remove port from their default ACS entry.

raj: Also flag: some RelayState values include an encoded fragment (e.g., '#/home') and in a few cases the IdP seems to build Recipient from their frontend URL which includes port. Add this to KB to warn customers about proxy/header differences.

oliver: After canary, I'll push verifier change to attempt each KeyDescriptor during signature verification (no preference by order) and add integration tests against metadata with mixed key ordering.

emma: Good. If canary shows errors going down we'll extend to 100% and close the ticket. If not, rollback and escalate to SRE to run live trace. Thanks all.

saml-checker-bot: Monitoring note: continuing to collect assertion fingerprints; will post summary in 30m.
